examples.ko: 이번 달 전기료가 너무 많이 나왔어요.
examples.en: This month's electricity bill came out really high.

examples.ko: 여름에는 에어컨 때문에 전기료가 두 배로 올라요.
examples.en: In summer the power bill doubles because of the air conditioner.

examples.ko: 전기료를 아끼려고 안 쓰는 플러그를 뽑아요.
examples.en: I unplug things I'm not using to save on the electricity bill.
Do you pay the electricity bill by automatic transfer every month?

examples.ko: 겨울에도 난방 때문에 전기료 걱정이 커요.
examples.en: Even in winter I worry about the power bill because of the heating.
The electricity bill notice came in the mailbox today.

explain: '전기 요금'을 줄인 말이고, 일상에서는 '전기세'라고도 말해요. '전기료가 나오다', '전기료를 내다', '전기료를 아끼다'처럼 '나오다·내다·아끼다'와 자주 같이 써요.
explain_en: It is a short form of '전기 요금', and in daily talk people also say '전기세'. It often goes with verbs like '나오다' (to come out), '내다' (to pay) and '아끼다' (to save), as in '전기료가 나오다'.

examples.ko: 요즘은 형과 제 키가 거의 같아졌어요.
examples.en: These days my older brother and I are almost the same height.

examples.ko: 나이가 들수록 제 말투가 엄마와 같아져요.
examples.en: The older I get, the more my way of speaking becomes like my mom's.

examples.ko: 두 팀의 점수가 같아져서 연장전을 했어요.
examples.en: The two teams' scores became tied, so they played extra time.

examples.ko: 가격이 같아지면 어느 쪽을 살 거예요?
examples.en: If the prices become the same, which one will you buy?

examples.ko: 오래 같이 살면 습관도 서로 같아질까요?
examples.en: If you live together for a long time, do your habits become alike too?

examples.ko: 아무리 설명해도 우리 의견은 같아지지 않아요.
examples.en: No matter how much I explain, our opinions don't become the same.

explain: 반대말은 '달라지다'예요. 비교하는 대상은 '~와/과 같아지다'처럼 '와/과'로 이어요. '똑같아지다'는 조금도 다르지 않다는 느낌이 더 강해요.
explain_en: The opposite is '달라지다' (to become different). The thing you compare with is linked by '와/과', as in '~와 같아지다'. '똑같아지다' feels stronger, as if there is no difference at all.

examples.ko: 이렇게 큰 상을 받다니 아직도 믿어지지 않아요.
examples.en: I still can't believe I won such a big prize.
Can you believe that you're graduating already?

examples.ko: 그 이야기는 너무 이상해서 쉽게 믿어지지 않았어요.
examples.en: That story was so strange that it was hard to believe.
Now that I've seen the photo myself, I can finally believe it.

examples.ko: 그 믿어지지 않는 일이 요즘 눈앞에서 벌어지고 있어요.
examples.en: That unbelievable thing is happening right before my eyes these days.

examples.ko: 저 사람이 한 말은 이상하게 믿어지는 힘이 있어요.
examples.en: What that person says has a strange power that makes you believe it.

explain: '믿다'와 달리 내 의지와 상관없이 마음에서 그렇게 느껴진다는 느낌이에요. 놀랍거나 실감이 안 날 때 '믿어지지 않아요'라고 말해요. 같은 뜻으로 '믿기지 않아요'도 써요.
explain_en: Unlike '믿다', it feels as if the belief happens in your heart regardless of your will. You say '믿어지지 않아요' when something is surprising or hard to take in. '믿기지 않아요' is used with the same meaning.

examples.ko: 이 신발은 커서 걸을 때마다 벗어져요.
examples.en: These shoes are big, so they come off every time I walk.
The wind blew hard and my hat came off.
My slippers came off while I was running, and it was embarrassing.

examples.ko: 장갑이 헐거워서 손에서 벗어질 것 같아요.
examples.en: The glove is loose, so it looks like it will slip off my hand.
My shoe came off and I lost one of them.

examples.ko: 양말이 벗어진 줄도 모르고 한참 걸었어요.
examples.en: I walked a long way without noticing that my sock had come off.

explain: '벗다'는 사람이 직접 하는 행동이고, '벗어지다'는 신발이나 모자가 저절로 빠질 때 써요. 같은 상황에 '벗겨지다'도 써요. 빠져나온다는 뜻의 '벗어나다'와 헷갈리지 마세요.
explain_en: '벗다' is something a person does on purpose, while '벗어지다' is for shoes or hats that come off by themselves. '벗겨지다' is also used in the same situations. Don't confuse it with '벗어나다', which means to get out of something.

examples.ko: 이 일은 제삼자가 끼어들 문제가 아니에요.
examples.en: This isn't a matter for a third party to step into.

examples.ko: 제삼자의 눈으로 보면 문제가 더 잘 보여요.
examples.en: The problem is easier to see through the eyes of a third party.

examples.ko: 계약 내용을 제삼자에게 알리면 안 돼요.
examples.en: You must not tell a third party the contents of the contract.

examples.ko: 둘 사이의 싸움에 제삼자까지 끌어들이지 마세요.
examples.en: Please don't drag a third party into the fight between you two.

examples.ko: 제삼자 입장에서 보면 둘 다 잘못했어요.
examples.en: From an outsider's point of view, both of you were wrong.

examples.ko: 사고가 났을 때 제삼자의 증언이 큰 도움이 됐어요.
examples.en: A third party's testimony was a big help when the accident happened.

explain: '당사자'의 반대말이에요. 법, 계약, 뉴스에서 '제삼자에게 알리다'처럼 나오고, 일상에서는 '남'이나 '다른 사람'이라고도 해요. '제3자'로 숫자를 써서 적기도 해요.
explain_en: It is the opposite of '당사자' (the person directly involved). It appears in law, contracts and the news, as in '제삼자에게 알리다', and in daily talk people also say '남' or '다른 사람'. It can also be written with a number, '제3자'.

examples.en: Yesterday I fell forward on the icy road and hurt my knee.
The child was running happily and fell flat on his face.
I tripped on a stone and almost fell on my face.
The cup tipped over and all the water spilled.
Be careful not to fall on the ice.
Since I fell on the stairs, I walk slowly.

explain: '넘어지다'는 쓰러지는 방향과 상관없이 쓰지만, '엎어지다'는 몸의 앞쪽이 바닥을 향해 앞으로 쓰러질 때 써요. 뒤로 쓰러지면 '자빠지다'를 쓰기도 해요. 컵이나 그릇이 뒤집혀 쏟아질 때도 써요.

phrases.example: 우리 집에서 학교까지는 엎어지면 코 닿을 데예요.
phrases.en: My house is a stone's throw from the school.
phrases.nuance_ko: 아주 가까운 거리를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to say that a place is very close.

explain_en: '넘어지다' can be used for any direction of falling, but '엎어지다' is for falling forward so the front of the body faces the ground. Falling backward can be '자빠지다'. It is also used when a cup or bowl is turned over and spills.

examples.en: Once in a while I get a call from an old friend.

examples.ko: 평소엔 집밥을 먹지만 가끔가다 외식도 해요.
examples.en: I usually eat at home, but occasionally I eat out too.

examples.ko: 저는 가끔가다 이른 아침에 산책을 해요.
examples.en: I sometimes go for a walk early in the morning.

examples.ko: 조용한 동네인데 가끔가다 오토바이 소리가 들려요.
examples.en: It's a quiet neighborhood, but now and then you hear a motorcycle.

examples.ko: 가끔가다 옛날 사진을 꺼내 보면 웃음이 나요.
examples.en: When I occasionally take out old photos, they make me smile.
That restaurant is delicious, so I think of it every now and then.

explain: '가끔'과 거의 같은 뜻이에요. '가끔가다'는 '이따금 한 번씩'이라는 느낌이 조금 더 있어요. 반대로 횟수가 많을 때는 '자주', '늘'을 써요.
explain_en: It means almost the same as '가끔'. '가끔가다' has a slightly stronger feel of 'once in a while'. For the opposite, when it happens a lot, use '자주' or '늘'.

examples.en: On Seollal we make tteokguk with garaetteok.

examples.ko: 갓 뽑은 가래떡을 조청에 찍어 먹었어요.
examples.en: I dipped freshly made garaetteok in grain syrup and ate it.

examples.ko: 가래떡을 얇게 썰어서 국에 넣어 주세요.
examples.en: Please slice the garaetteok thin and put it in the soup.
Garaetteok is chewy when you eat it while it's warm.

examples.ko: 우리 가래떡 구워서 꿀에 찍어 먹을까요?
examples.en: Shall we grill the garaetteok and dip it in honey?

examples.ko: 가래떡의 가운데를 뚝 잘라 친구와 나눠 먹었어요.
examples.en: I cut the garaetteok in the middle and shared it with my friend.

explain: 길쭉하고 흰 떡이에요. 얇게 썰어서 떡국에 넣거나, 구워서 꿀이나 조청에 찍어 먹어요. 설날 음식으로 많이 떠올려요.
explain_en: It is a long, white rice cake. People slice it thin for tteokguk, or grill it and dip it in honey or grain syrup. Many Koreans think of it as a Seollal food.

examples.en: The moon is hidden behind the clouds, so I can't see it.

examples.ko: 앞사람 키가 커서 화면이 반쯤 가려졌어요.
examples.en: The person in front is tall, so half the screen is blocked.

examples.ko: 나무에 가려져서 간판이 잘 안 보여요.
examples.en: The sign is hidden by the trees and is hard to see.

examples.ko: 가방을 이불로 덮었지만 다 가려지지 않았어요.
examples.en: I covered the bag with a blanket, but it wasn't completely hidden.

examples.ko: 이 커튼을 치면 창문이 완전히 가려질까요?
examples.en: If I close this curtain, will the window be fully covered?

examples.ko: 큰 건물에 가려져서 바다가 안 보여요.
examples.en: The sea is hidden by the big building, so I can't see it.

explain: '가리다'의 피동으로, 무엇이 앞을 막아서 안 보이게 되었다는 느낌이에요. 단순히 '안 보이다'보다 막고 있는 것이 있다는 점이 달라요. '승부가 가려지다'처럼 결과가 분명하게 정해질 때도 써요.
explain_en: It is the passive of '가리다', and it feels like something is standing in front and blocking the view. Compared with plain '안 보이다', it points to something that is blocking. It is also used when a result gets clearly decided, as in '승부가 가려지다'.

examples.en: Children's powder medicine is mixed with water and taken.
If the powder medicine is bitter, I mix it with syrup.

examples.ko: 이 약은 알약 말고 가루약으로 주세요.
examples.en: Please give me this medicine as powder, not as pills.

examples.ko: 가루약을 먹을 때는 사레들리지 않게 조심하세요.
examples.en: Be careful not to choke when you take powder medicine.

examples.ko: 감기에 걸려서 병원에서 가루약을 받아 왔어요.
examples.en: I caught a cold and got powder medicine at the hospital.

examples.ko: 가루약이 입안에 남아서 물을 한 컵 더 마셨어요.
examples.en: The powder stayed in my mouth, so I drank another cup of water.

explain: 병원이나 약국에서 '가루약으로 주세요'처럼 약의 모양을 고를 때 써요. '알약', '물약', '시럽'과 짝으로 같이 나와요. 아이들 약은 가루약으로 받는 경우가 있어요.
explain_en: You use it at the hospital or pharmacy to choose the form of medicine, as in '가루약으로 주세요'. It comes as a set with '알약' (pill), '물약' (liquid medicine) and '시럽' (syrup). Children's medicine is sometimes given as powder.

examples.en: My house is heated with a gas boiler.

examples.ko: 가스보일러가 고장 나서 샤워를 못 했어요.
examples.en: The gas boiler broke, so I couldn't take a shower.

examples.ko: 겨울이 오기 전에 가스보일러를 점검해야 해요.
examples.en: We need to check the gas boiler before winter comes.
Please lower the gas boiler temperature a little.
There's a strange noise coming from the gas boiler.

examples.ko: 이사 간 집에 새 가스보일러가 있었어요.
examples.en: The house I moved into had a new gas boiler.

explain: 일상에서는 그냥 '보일러'라고 말할 때가 많아요. '보일러를 켜다/틀다/끄다'처럼 써요. 기름을 쓰는 '기름보일러'와 구분할 때 '가스보일러'라고 해요.
explain_en: In daily talk people often just say '보일러'. You use it like '보일러를 켜다/틀다/끄다' (turn on/off). You say '가스보일러' to tell it apart from an oil boiler, '기름보일러'.

examples.en: I had a lot of things in my heart that I wanted to say.

examples.ko: 가슴속 울분을 글로 풀어내자 마음이 한결 가벼워졌어요.
examples.en: Once I let out the anger in my heart through writing, my mind felt much lighter.

examples.ko: 그 말을 가슴속 깊이 새겨 두었어요.
examples.en: I engraved those words deep in my heart.
It feels refreshing, as if my chest were wide open.

examples.ko: 가슴속에만 담아 두지 말고 이야기해 보세요.
examples.en: Don't keep it only inside your heart. Try talking about it.

examples.ko: 아버지의 마지막 말씀이 아직도 가슴속에 남아 있어요.
examples.en: My father's last words still remain in my heart.

explain: '마음속'과 비슷하지만 '가슴속'은 울분이나 그리움처럼 가슴이 답답하거나 벅찬 감정에 잘 어울려요. 생각이나 기억은 '머릿속'이라고 해요. 보통 '가슴속에', '가슴속 깊이'처럼 써요.
explain_en: It is similar to '마음속', but '가슴속' fits feelings that make the chest tight or full, like anger or longing. Thoughts and memories go in '머릿속'. It is usually used as '가슴속에' or '가슴속 깊이'.

examples.en: Please mark the wrong problems with a cross.
The teacher put a cross on the wrong answer.
If it's right, make a circle. If it's wrong, make a cross.
Don't put a cross in this box.
There are so many crosses on my test paper that I'm upset.
A cross mark is also called an X mark.

explain: 동그라미(○)와 반대로 틀렸다는 표시를 말해요. '가위표를 하다/치다'처럼 써요. 같은 모양을 '엑스(X) 표시'라고도 해요.
explain_en: It is the opposite of a circle (○) and shows that an answer is wrong. You say '가위표를 하다/치다'. The same mark is also called an 'X 표시'.

examples.en: This restaurant was made by remodeling a house.

examples.ko: 골목 안에 있는 가정집에서 하숙을 해요.
examples.en: I lodge at a private house in the alley.
Since it's a private house, it's quieter than an office.
This shop looks like an ordinary house.
Please keep a fire extinguisher even in an ordinary home.

examples.ko: 옛 가정집을 카페로 바꾼 곳이 많아요.
examples.en: There are many places where an old house was turned into a cafe.

explain: 가게, 사무실, 학교 같은 건물과 구분해서 사람이 사는 집을 말할 때 써요. '일반 가정집', '가정집을 개조하다'처럼 자주 나와요. 그냥 '집'이라고 해도 되지만 건물의 용도를 강조할 때 '가정집'이라고 해요.
explain_en: You use it to talk about a house where people live, as opposed to a shop, office or school. It appears in phrases like '일반 가정집' and '가정집을 개조하다'. You can just say '집', but '가정집' stresses the building's use.

examples.en: Wearing leather clothes in winter keeps you warm.
Leather clothes are hard to take care of if they get rained on.
My father still wears his old leather clothes.
The leather clothes were too heavy, so I didn't buy them.
I bought a jacket at a leather clothing shop.

examples.ko: 가죽옷은 집에서 빨지 말고 세탁소에 맡기세요.
examples.en: Don't wash leather clothes at home. Take them to the cleaner's.

explain: 가죽으로 만든 옷을 통틀어 말해요. 구체적인 옷은 '가죽 재킷', '가죽 바지'처럼 가죽을 앞에 붙여 말해요. 관리는 보통 '세탁소에 맡기다'고 해요.
explain_en: It is a general word for clothes made of leather. For a specific item, people put '가죽' in front, like '가죽 재킷' or '가죽 바지'. For care, people usually say '세탁소에 맡기다' (leave it at the cleaner's).

examples.en: On busy mornings I simply get by with bread.

examples.ko: 이 앱으로 간편히 송금할 수 있어요.
examples.en: You can send money easily with this app.
I packed light and left for the trip.
Please come dressed casually.

examples.ko: 간편히 먹을 수 있는 도시락을 샀어요.
examples.en: I bought a lunch box that is easy to eat.
Is there a convenient way to submit the documents?

explain: '간편하게'와 같은 뜻이에요. 말할 때는 '간편하게'를 쓰기도 하고, '간편히'는 안내문이나 광고 문구에서도 볼 수 있어요. 형용사는 '간편하다'예요.
explain_en: It means the same as '간편하게'. In speech people also say '간편하게', and '간편히' can be seen in notices and ads. The adjective is '간편하다'.

examples.ko: 땀에 젖은 아이에게 새 옷을 갈아입혔어요.
examples.en: I changed the sweaty child into new clothes.
Mom changed the baby into pajamas.
I played by changing the doll into pretty clothes.
I'll help change the patient into the hospital gown.
They got wet from the rain, so please change their clothes quickly.
Every morning I wake up my little brother and change his clothes.

explain: '갈아입다'는 자기가 옷을 바꿔 입는 것이고, '갈아입히다'는 다른 사람의 옷을 대신 갈아입게 해 주는 거예요. '아이에게 옷을 갈아입히다'처럼 '~에게 ~을'로 써요. 아기나 아이, 환자에게 주로 써요.
explain_en: '갈아입다' is changing your own clothes, while '갈아입히다' is changing someone else's clothes for them. It is used like '아이에게 옷을 갈아입히다' with '~에게 ~을'. It is mostly used for babies, children and patients.

examples.ko: 감나무 가지에 까치 한 쌍이 둥지를 틀었어요.
examples.en: A pair of magpies built a nest on the persimmon tree branch.

examples.ko: 담 너머 이웃집 감나무에서 감이 익어 가요.
examples.en: The persimmons are ripening on the neighbor's tree over the wall.

examples.ko: 우리 집 감나무에 감이 많이 열렸어요.
examples.en: Our persimmon tree has a lot of fruit.

examples.ko: 우리 집 감나무가 유독 크고 감도 커요.
examples.en: Our persimmon tree is especially big, and the persimmons are big too.

examples.ko: 가을이면 감나무에 주황색 감이 주렁주렁 달려요.
examples.en: In autumn, orange persimmons hang in clusters from the tree.

examples.ko: 할머니 댁 마당에는 오래된 감나무가 있어요.
examples.en: There is an old persimmon tree in my grandmother's yard.

explain: '감'은 열매이고 '감나무'는 그 열매가 열리는 나무예요. '감이 열리다', '감이 익다'와 함께 써요. 시골 마당이나 담장 풍경을 말할 때 나와요.
explain_en: '감' is the fruit and '감나무' is the tree it grows on. It is used with '감이 열리다' (fruit grows) and '감이 익다' (fruit ripens). It comes up when describing a country yard or a fence scene.

examples.en: After work I went to eat gamjatang with a friend.
The meat on the bones is delicious in gamjatang.
On cold days I think of hot gamjatang.

examples.ko: 감자탕 이 인분에 공기밥 하나 주세요.
examples.en: Please give us two servings of gamjatang and one bowl of rice.
I ate gamjatang and even fried rice, so I'm full.
This shop's gamjatang has a spicy, rich broth.

explain: 돼지 등뼈를 넣고 얼큰하게 끓인 탕이에요. 보통 큰 냄비에 여럿이 나눠 먹고, 다 먹은 뒤에 밥을 볶아 먹기도 해요. 식당에서는 '감자탕 중짜 하나 주세요'처럼 크기로 시켜요.
explain_en: It is a spicy stew boiled with pork backbone. People usually share a big pot, and sometimes fry rice in the leftover broth. At restaurants you order by size, like '감자탕 중짜 하나 주세요'.

examples.ko: 이 가방은 디자인이 좋지만 너무 값비싸요.
examples.en: This bag has a nice design, but it's too expensive.
The thought matters more than an expensive gift.
I bought expensive clothes and regretted it.
The food here is pricey, but the taste is guaranteed.

examples.ko: 저 가게는 물건이 다 값비싸서 구경만 했어요.
examples.en: Everything in that shop is expensive, so I just looked around.
He is wearing a watch that looks expensive.

explain: '비싸다'와 비슷하지만 '값비싼 보석'처럼 뒤에 명사를 꾸밀 때 고급스럽고 귀한 느낌이 있어요. 반대말은 '값싸다'예요. '값비싼, 값비싸요, 값비싸서'로 활용해요.
explain_en: It is like '비싸다', but when it modifies a noun, as in '값비싼 보석', it feels luxurious and precious. The opposite is '값싸다'. It conjugates as '값비싼, 값비싸요, 값비싸서'.

examples.en: A newborn baby wakes up often all day long.
A newborn baby was born next door.

examples.ko: 갓난아기를 안을 때는 목을 받쳐 줘야 해요.
examples.en: When you hold a newborn baby, you need to support the neck.
I could hear a newborn baby crying all night.

examples.ko: 갓난아기 때 제 사진을 보니 신기해요.
examples.en: It's amazing to see a picture of me as a newborn.
My nephew is a newborn, so I came to buy a gift.

explain: 막 태어난 아기를 말해요. '갓난아이', '갓난애'도 같은 뜻으로 써요. 병원에서 쓰는 '신생아'는 조금 딱딱하게 들려요.
explain_en: It refers to a baby who has just been born. '갓난아이' and '갓난애' are used with the same meaning. '신생아', used in hospitals, sounds a bit more formal.

en: be forced; be pressured; be coerced

examples.en: I was forced to apologize and it made me feel bad.

examples.ko: 굴복을 강요받은 직원이 결국 회사를 그만두었어요.
examples.en: The employee who was pressured to give in finally quit the company.

examples.ko: 아이들은 공부를 너무 강요받으면 흥미를 잃어요.
examples.en: Children lose interest if they are pushed too hard to study.

examples.ko: 저는 한 번도 결혼을 강요받은 적이 없어요.
examples.en: I have never been pressured to get married.
A friend pressured me to lend him money.
If you feel pressured, it's okay to refuse.

explain: '강요하다'의 반대편에서 하는 말이에요. 'A에게 B를 강요받다'처럼 써요. '강요당하다'도 비슷한데, '-당하다'는 억울하고 힘든 느낌이 더 강해요.
explain_en: It describes the side that receives what '강요하다' (to force) does. It is used like 'A에게 B를 강요받다'. '강요당하다' is similar, but '-당하다' feels more unfair and painful.

examples.en: Tomorrow is the school's anniversary, so we don't go to school.
I'm going out with my friends on the school anniversary.

examples.ko: 우리 학교 개교기념일은 시월 이십 일이에요.
examples.en: Our school's anniversary is on October 20th.
It's a pity that the school anniversary falls on a weekend.
Thanks to the school anniversary, the holiday got longer.
On the school anniversary, the library is closed too.

explain: 학교가 처음 세워진 날을 기념하는 날이에요. 날짜는 학교마다 달라요. 그날을 쉬는 날로 정한 학교도 있고 그렇지 않은 학교도 있어요.
explain_en: It is the day that marks when a school was founded. The date is different for each school. Some schools make it a day off and some don't.

examples.ko: 초등학교 육 년 동안 개근을 했어요.
examples.en: I had perfect attendance for six years of elementary school.
I went to school even when sick to get the perfect attendance award.
My younger brother has perfect attendance, with no lateness or absences.

examples.ko: 일 년 내내 학교를 개근하는 게 쉽지 않아요.
examples.en: It's not easy to attend school every day all year.
I had perfect attendance this semester too.
The teacher praised me for having perfect attendance.

explain: 학교에 하루도 빠지지 않고 나온 것을 말해요. '개근하다', '개근상'으로 자주 써요. 반대로 빠진 날은 '결석'이라고 해요.
explain_en: It means attending school without missing a single day. It is often used as '개근하다' and '개근상' (perfect attendance award). A day you miss is called '결석'.

examples.en: I was born in the year of the dog, and my older brother was born in the year of the horse.
People born in the year of the dog gathered.
This meeting is only for people born in the year of the dog.
I was glad to meet someone with the same zodiac sign, the dog.
Are you born in the year of the dog? I didn't know.

examples.ko: 개띠는 열두 띠 중에서 열한 번째예요.
examples.en: The dog is the eleventh of the twelve zodiac animals.

explain: 태어난 해의 동물로 말하는 열두 띠 중 개예요. 한국에서는 나이를 물을 때 '무슨 띠예요?'라고 묻기도 해요. '말띠', '용띠'처럼 '동물+띠'로 말해요.
explain_en: It is the dog in the twelve zodiac animals, based on the year you were born. In Korea people sometimes ask about age with '무슨 띠예요?'. Other signs are said as 'animal + 띠', like '말띠' and '용띠'.

examples.en: I found a big ant nest in the yard.
Ants are going into the nest entrance in a line.

examples.ko: 아이들이 개미집을 막대기로 건드리지 않게 하세요.
examples.en: Please don't let the kids poke the ant nest with a stick.

examples.ko: 비가 오기 전에는 개미집 근처가 바빠 보여요.
examples.en: Before it rains, the area around the ant nest looks busy.
An ant nest stretches long underground.
Who made this ant nest?

explain: 개미가 사는 곳이에요. 땅속에 판 구멍은 '개미굴'이라고도 해요. '개미집을 짓다', '개미집을 건드리다'처럼 써요.
explain_en: It is the place where ants live. A hole dug underground is also called '개미굴'. It is used like '개미집을 짓다' (build) and '개미집을 건드리다' (disturb).

examples.ko: 새 앱의 개발비가 생각보다 많이 들었어요.
examples.en: The new app's development cost was more than I expected.
To cut development costs, we didn't hire more staff.
I heard new drug development costs hundreds of billions of won.

examples.ko: 이 게임은 개발비만 오십억 원이 넘었어요.
examples.en: The development cost of this game alone exceeded five billion won.
The government supports technology development costs.

examples.ko: 개발비 때문에 가격을 올릴 수밖에 없어요.
examples.en: Because of the development cost, we have no choice but to raise the price.

explain: 제품이나 기술을 새로 만드는 데 드는 돈이에요. '생활비', '교육비'처럼 '~비'가 붙은 말이에요. 'N 개발비'처럼 앞에 개발 대상을 붙여요.
explain_en: It is the money spent on creating a new product or technology. It is built like '생활비' and '교육비', with '비' attached. You put the thing developed in front, like 'N 개발비'.

examples.en: My father is an owner-driver taxi driver.
I make my living running a private taxi.
An owner-driver taxi doesn't belong to a company.
At night it's hard to catch an owner-driver taxi.
I took a private taxi all the way to the airport.
The private taxi driver knows the roads well.

explain: 회사 소속이 아니라 기사 본인이 면허를 가지고 운행하는 택시예요. 회사에서 운영하는 '법인택시'와 구분해서 말해요. 보통 '개인택시 기사'라고 해요.
explain_en: It is a taxi run by a driver who holds the license personally, not by a company. It is distinguished from '법인택시', which a company operates. People usually say '개인택시 기사'.

examples.ko: 단체 여행에서는 개인행동을 하면 안 돼요.
examples.en: You shouldn't act on your own on a group trip.
Others had to wait because of one person's solo behavior.

examples.ko: 점심 후에는 한 시간 개인행동 시간이에요.
examples.en: After lunch there is one hour of free time on your own.

examples.ko: 저는 혼자 하는 개인행동이 더 편해요.
examples.en: I'm more comfortable doing things on my own.

examples.ko: 선생님이 수학여행에서 개인행동을 하지 말라고 하셨어요.
examples.en: The teacher told us not to go off on our own on the school trip.

examples.ko: 개인행동을 하고 싶으면 미리 말해 주세요.
examples.en: If you want to act on your own, please tell us in advance.

explain: 단체와 따로 혼자 움직이는 행동을 말해요. 단체 여행이나 학교 행사에서 '개인행동은 하지 마세요'라는 말을 많이 들어요. 반대로 함께 움직이는 건 '단체행동'이에요.
explain_en: It refers to acting alone, separate from the group. On group trips and school events you hear '개인행동은 하지 마세요'. Moving together is '단체행동'.

examples.en: There is a doghouse in one corner of the yard.
My father built a doghouse himself for us.
When it rained, the puppy went into the doghouse.
The doghouse got too small, so I switched to a bigger one.
I spread a blanket inside the doghouse.

examples.ko: 새 개집이 마음에 들었는지 강아지가 안 나와요.
examples.en: The puppy must like the new doghouse because it won't come out.

explain: 개가 쉬고 자는 작은 집이에요. 집 안에서 키우는 강아지의 집은 '강아지 집'이라고 부르기도 해요. '개집을 만들다', '개집에 들어가다'처럼 써요.
explain_en: It is the small house where a dog rests and sleeps. For a puppy kept indoors, people also say '강아지 집'. It is used like '개집을 만들다' and '개집에 들어가다'.

examples.en: You shouldn't tease a friend by calling him a liar.

examples.ko: 그 애는 거짓말쟁이라서 아무도 안 믿어요.
examples.en: That kid is a liar, so nobody believes him.

examples.ko: 아이가 거짓말쟁이라는 누명을 쓸까 봐 부모는 끝까지 이야기를 들어 주었어요.
examples.en: Fearing the child would be wrongly called a liar, the parents listened to the whole story.
The shepherd boy became known as a liar.
Don't make me out to be a liar.
I was upset to be called a liar by a friend.

explain: '-쟁이'는 그런 버릇이나 특징이 있는 사람을 가리키고 약간 놀리는 말투예요. 어른에게 직접 쓰면 실례가 될 수 있어요. 비슷한 말로 '거짓말꾼'이 있어요.
explain_en: '-쟁이' points to a person with that habit or trait, and it has a slightly teasing tone. Using it directly to an adult can be rude. A similar word is '거짓말꾼'.

examples.en: Is there a health food store near here?

examples.ko: 건강식품을 사라고 강권하는 바람에 모임에 나가기가 싫어졌어요.
examples.en: They kept pushing me to buy health supplements, so I stopped wanting to go to the meetings.
I picked out health food to give to my parents.
Everyday eating habits matter more than health food.

examples.ko: 이 건강식품은 하루에 한 알만 먹어요.
examples.en: You take just one tablet of this health supplement a day.

examples.ko: 건강식품을 살 때는 성분을 꼭 확인하세요.
examples.en: When buying health food, be sure to check the ingredients.

explain: 비타민, 홍삼처럼 건강을 위해 먹는 식품을 말해요. '건강기능식품'이라고도 해요. 명절이나 어버이날에 부모님께 선물로 드리기도 해요.
explain_en: It refers to food taken for health, such as vitamins and red ginseng. It is also called '건강기능식품'. People sometimes give it to their parents as a gift at holidays or Parents' Day.

examples.en: Please stay in good health.
Grandma, please live a long and healthy life.

examples.ko: 건강히 잘 지내고 있으니 걱정 마세요.
examples.en: I'm doing well and healthy, so don't worry.
Let's stay healthy until we meet next time.
I'm so thankful that the child is growing up healthy.
I promised that I would come back safe and healthy.

explain: '건강하게'와 같은 뜻이고, 편지나 안부 인사에서 '건강히 지내세요'로 많이 써요. 보통 '지내다·살다·자라다·돌아오다'와 같이 나와요. 형용사는 '건강하다'예요.
explain_en: It means the same as '건강하게' and is used in letters and greetings, as in '건강히 지내세요'. It usually goes with verbs like '지내다', '살다', '자라다' and '돌아오다'. The adjective is '건강하다'.

examples.en: I looked across through the window at the house opposite.

examples.ko: 강 건너편 마을을 건너다보니 불빛이 반짝여요.
examples.en: Looking across at the village on the other side of the river, lights sparkle.

examples.ko: 친구가 길 건너에서 이쪽을 건너다보고 있어요.
examples.en: My friend is looking this way from across the road.

examples.ko: 아이가 창가에 서서 강 건너편 산을 건너다봐요.
examples.en: The child stands by the window and looks across the river at the mountain.

examples.ko: 건너다보면 바다 쪽에 작은 섬이 보여요.
examples.en: If you look across, you can see a small island near the sea.

examples.ko: 그 사람은 말없이 저를 건너다보기만 했어요.
examples.en: He just looked across at me without saying a word.

explain: 멀리 떨어진 맞은편을 바라볼 때 써요. 위쪽을 향해 보는 '쳐다보다'와 달라요. 담이나 울타리 너머로 보는 건 '넘겨다보다'라고 해요.
explain_en: You use it when looking at something far away on the opposite side. It is different from '쳐다보다', which means looking up at something. Looking over a wall or fence is '넘겨다보다'.

examples.en: I was handed a present by my friend.
I took the receipt from the clerk and went out.

examples.ko: 모르는 사람이 주는 음식은 건네받지 마세요.
examples.en: Don't accept food handed to you by a stranger.

examples.ko: 열쇠를 건네받는 순간 이사 온 실감이 났어요.
examples.en: The moment I was handed the key, it felt real that I had moved in.
The student who was handed the microphone sang a song.
When you are handed the documents, please check them right away.

explain: '건네주다'의 반대로, 받는 사람 입장에서 말해요. '받다'보다 상대가 손으로 직접 내밀어 준 느낌이 있어요. 'A에게서 B를 건네받다'처럼 써요.
explain_en: It is the opposite of '건네주다' and is said from the receiver's point of view. Compared with '받다', it feels like the other person held it out and handed it over. It is used like 'A에게서 B를 건네받다'.

examples.en: Every weekend I mop the living room floor with a cloth.
You need to sweep and then wipe the room to get rid of dust.
I scrubbed hard with a cloth, and the floor got clean.

examples.ko: 제가 걸레질할 테니까 청소기를 돌려 주세요.
examples.en: I'll wipe the floor, so please run the vacuum cleaner.

examples.ko: 부엌 바닥은 물걸레로 걸레질하면 잘 닦여요.
examples.en: The kitchen floor gets clean if you wipe it with a wet cloth.
Keep the windows open while you wipe the floor.

explain: 걸레로 바닥이나 가구를 닦는 일이에요. '걸레질을 하다'와 '걸레질하다'를 둘 다 써요. 보통 '쓸기·청소기'로 먼지를 치운 다음에 해요.
explain_en: It is wiping the floor or furniture with a cloth. Both '걸레질을 하다' and '걸레질하다' are used. It usually comes after removing dust by sweeping or vacuuming.

examples.en: The sky turned black and then the rain poured down.
Her black hair is shiny.
The night sea was entirely black.

examples.ko: 눈 밑이 검은빛으로 보일 만큼 피곤해요.
examples.en: I'm so tired that the skin under my eyes looks dark.

examples.ko: 이 가죽은 오래 쓰면 검은빛이 더 깊어져요.
examples.en: This leather's black gets deeper the longer you use it.
Dark clouds are gathering.

explain: '검은색'은 색 이름이고, '검은빛'은 어떤 것에서 나는 어두운 색의 기운을 말할 때 잘 어울려요. 일상 대화에서는 '까만색'이나 '검정색'을 더 쉽게 말해요. '빛' 때문에 약간 글에서 쓰는 느낌이 있어요.
explain_en: '검은색' is the name of the color, while '검은빛' fits when describing the dark tint something gives off. In everyday talk people simply say '까만색' or '검정색'. The word '빛' gives it a slightly written feel.

examples.en: I add black beans to the rice when I cook it.
I drink black soybean milk every morning.
My mom soaked black beans and made braised beans.

examples.ko: 검정콩은 하루 전에 물에 불려 두세요.
examples.en: Soak the black beans in water a day before.
The black beans made the rice color darker.
I bought a bag of black beans at the market.

explain: '검은콩'이라고도 해요. 밥에 넣어 먹거나, 조림이나 두유로 만들어 먹어요. '검정'은 색을 나타내는 명사예요.
explain_en: It is also called '검은콩'. People put it in rice, or make it into braised beans or soy milk. '검정' is a noun that refers to the color black.

examples.en: My little brother scared me with a ghost story.

examples.ko: 아이한테 겁주지 말고 차분히 설명해 주세요.
examples.en: Don't scare the child. Please explain calmly.
I said it to scare him, but he was really frightened.

examples.ko: 형이 큰 소리로 겁줘서 깜짝 놀랐어요.
examples.en: My older brother scared me with a loud voice and I was startled.
That dog scares people by barking.
There is no one you may scare as a joke.

explain: 상대가 겁먹게 만든다는 뜻으로, '겁먹다'와 짝이에요. '겁을 주다'처럼 띄어 쓰는 표현도 같이 써요. 활용은 '겁주어/겁줘'로 해요.
explain_en: It pairs with '겁먹다' (to get scared), as it makes the other person scared. The spaced form '겁을 주다' is used too. It conjugates as '겁주어/겁줘'.

examples.en: It's better to care about substance than appearance.
Even if it looks great outside, the inside matters.
This fruit doesn't look good, but it tastes delicious.
Don't judge just by outward appearance.
They only changed the outside, so it looks like a new car.
The two products look alike on the outside, so I got confused.

explain: '겉모습'과 거의 같고, 물건이나 음식의 바깥 모양을 말할 때 잘 어울려요. 사람에게는 '겉모습'이나 '외모'도 써요. 반대로 안쪽은 '속'이라고 해요.
explain_en: It is almost the same as '겉모습' and fits the outer look of objects and food. For people, '겉모습' or '외모' is also used. The inside is called '속'.

examples.ko: 선물 겉포장이 너무 예뻐서 뜯기 아까워요.
examples.en: The gift wrapping is so pretty that I hate to tear it.
You have to tear the outer wrapping to find the manual inside.

examples.ko: 이 과일은 겉포장만 화려하고 양은 적어요.
examples.en: This fruit has fancy outer packaging but there is little in it.
Please take off the outer wrapping and then throw it away.
Please exchange products whose outer packaging is torn.
The expiration date is written on the outer packaging.

explain: 제품을 감싼 바깥쪽 포장이에요. 안쪽에 따로 싼 '속포장'과 구분해서 말해요. 선물이나 상품을 살 때 '겉포장만 해 주세요'처럼 말할 수 있어요.
explain_en: It is the outermost wrapping around a product. It is distinguished from the inner '속포장', which wraps the item separately inside. When buying a gift or goods you can say something like '겉포장만 해 주세요'.
